long_biography.plain_text:
As a teenager newly arrived in Adelaide, Stefan Ackerie learned English at night school and worked in his father’s salon. He opened a shop of his own while still an apprentice, employing a qualified senior hairdresser because he was too young to operate it alone. Moves through regional Queensland brought him to Brisbane, where the self-named Stefan salons became his enduring business.

Ackerie paired salon expansion with a proprietary haircare range and a televised styling programme. He also developed a training system that made the company a major educator and employer of apprentices. Away from the salon floor, he built Jo Jo’s into a well-known Brisbane restaurant and preserved the city’s Expo-era Skyneedle, reflecting a broader interest in hospitality and civic landmarks.
